prohibitions: Never create, edit or delete repositories
guide.summary: Forgejo documents OAuth2 Authorization Code with PKCE for third-party apps acting for a user. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token can run any action the user can, and read-only behavior must be enforced by the app.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Forgejo documents OAuth2 Authorization Code for user-consented third-party apps
findings.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider so third-party applications can access its resources with user consent. Apps use the Authorization Code grant with PKCE support, and the app must be registered in user settings first.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects an individual account on their own Forgejo instance using OAuth.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.
Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:

OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

findings.title: OAuth2 tokens have no scope restriction and act with the user's full rights
findings.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens, and they can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git actions. Scoped personal access tokens are a separate mechanism and are not an OAuth grant.
findings.appliesWhen: The app uses OAuth access tokens to call the API.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: Register a client (confidential or public) and send Bearer tokens to the API
findings.detail: Forgejo supports confidential and public clients. OAuth access tokens are accepted in the Authorization: Bearer header or as token/access_token query parameters. The redirect URI and client type must match the registration.
findings.appliesWhen: The app is set up for customer instances.

evidence.quote: Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers

findings.title: Read-only is an app-enforced constraint, not a token boundary
findings.detail: The OAuth token can be used for write operations, so the app must only call GET routes. Customers should be told the token itself is not read-only.
findings.appliesWhen: The app must never create, edit or delete repositories.

evidence.quote: execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.
Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: Read repository access via token scope read:repository
findings.detail: read:repository grants read access to repository operations, including repository listing endpoints under /repos/*. Use it for the read-only repository search. Avoid write:repository, which allows creating, editing and deleting repositories. Note that personal/API token scopes are distinct from OAuth2 tokens, which do not implement scopes and act with the user's full rights.
findings.appliesWhen: Personal or scoped access token is used to list repositories.

evidence.quote: read:repository Grants read access to repository operations, such as getting repository files, releases, and collaborators.
repository /repos/* API routes except /repos/issues/* : Repository file, pull-request, and release operations.
write:repository Grants read/write/delete access to repository operations, such as getting and updating repository files, creating pull requests, and updating collaborators.

steps.title: Register the OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Create a user-level OAuth2 application at the instance settings page for applications. Use a public client with PKCE for the first test, with the redirect URI for the test callback. The instance base URL is a user-provided input.
steps.doneWhen: The application shows a Client ID and the redirect URI is saved for the chosen client type.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Note Please ensure you have registered your OAuth application as a public client.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer Forgejo HTTPS origin, user-provided
CLIENT_ID: copied from the application page after registration
REDIRECT_URI: test callback URL configured in the app

steps.title: Open the authorization URL and confirm the callback
steps.detail: Send the person to the documented authorization endpoint with PKCE parameters, approve access, and check that the redirect returns a code and matching state.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URI receives code and state values that match the values sent.

INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: List visible repositories (first page)
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/repos/search with limit and page=1 and no is_private filter so private repositories the user can access are included by default. Read only. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns repository names in $.data[].name and the Link and x-total-count headers are captured. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.

steps.title: Follow the next page of visible repositories
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/repos/search, following the rel=next URL from the Link header unchanged, until no rel=next link remains. Stop only on the documented end condition, not on an empty page. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.
steps.doneWhen: All pages are read until no rel=next link remains and the collected count equals x-total-count. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

fields: NEXT_PAGE_URL: rel=next URL from the prior Link header, used unchanged
ACCESS_TOKEN: same token as the first page
